cold_open.hook: Victoria's Secret just jumped 40% on earnings—turns out the internet's favorite punching bag figured out how to sell things to actual humans again.

markets.macro_note: Mega-cap tech rolling over (MSFT -4.17%, GOOGL -3.86%) while small-cap and semiconductor plays catch a bid; VIX cooling suggests no panic underneath.

big_story.story_title: Victoria's Secret shares spike 40% after big earnings beat, raised sales outlook
big_story.angle: A brand that spent five years being a cultural punchline just proved the turnaround thesis works—what changed operationally, and is this a one-quarter pop or a real reset?

quick_hits.angle: HPE's 19% surge on blowout earnings is the infrastructure-AI trade working exactly as advertised—data center capex is real money, not hype.
Palo Alto Networks rallying on earnings because AI actually *is* helping cybersecurity (not replacing it)—the rare case where the hype cycle and fundamentals align.
Next-gen handheld gaming device review incoming—the portable console market is choosing violence against Nintendo's handheld dominance again.
Microsoft Build 2026 announcements: seven big reveals, probably four of them are 'AI but slightly different' and one will actually matter in 18 months.

odd_thing.joke_angle: Cyberdecks are having a moment—basically steampunk laptops for people who think their MacBook Air is too complicit in the surveillance economy. It's the Crocs IPO of computing.

sign_off.callback_target: Victoria's Secret's 40% pop—because sometimes the internet's favorite brand to dunk on just decides to actually execute.
